tagline: Mountain lakes, river crossings and a road reshaped above Horseshoe Bend
intro: The Payette River Scenic Byway follows Idaho 55 between New Meadows and Eagle, linking mountain valleys with the Payette River canyon. The Federal Highway Administration lists it as a National Scenic Byway and describes foothills, forests and open valleys, with access to rafting, kayaking and fishing. Its archived guide allows 2.5 hours for the 112-mile drive.

The highway acquired its present number in 1967, replacing State Highways 72 and 15. Its alignment continued to change: landslides and extended closures had troubled the curving road west of Horseshoe Bend Hill. The old roadway crossed part of an ancient lake, where dozens of springs fed water beneath it and undermined the road. A new multilane grade was completed in late 1991, changing the climb between the river and Spring Valley Summit.

From New Meadows, drive through Meadows and climb the narrow, twisting canyon toward Goose Creek Summit, then descend to McCall and Payette Lake. Turn south through Long Valley, passing Donnelly and the east shore of Cascade Reservoir before Cascade. Beyond Round Valley, the route crosses the 1933 Rainbow Bridge and passes Smiths Ferry and Banks on its way to Horseshoe Bend. The final climb gains 1,600 feet to Spring Valley Summit before the descent toward Eagle.

moments.title: McCall
moments.text: McCall occupies the lake’s southern shore. Payette Lake gave McCall a place in the movies: Northwest Passage was filmed here in 1938, with Idaho forests standing in for New England and the Upper Midwest. The film reached theaters in 1940, but visitors had been coming long before the cameras. A railroad reached McCall in 1914, making the lake more accessible as a destination for summer and winter recreation. The water itself has an older origin: glacial activity formed the lake. At its southwest corner, a small dam completed in 1943 regulates the outflow for irrigation.

moments.title: Smiths Ferry
moments.text: The North Fork briefly widens and calms at Smiths Ferry, where the place name preserves an earlier way across the water. Clinton Meyers established a ferry here in 1887 to carry livestock to summer pasture in Round and Long Valleys. Freighters used it too; Meyers sold the crossing to Jim Smith in 1891, giving Smiths Ferry its name. Idaho 55 now passes through the community and crosses the river on the Rainbow Bridge beyond it when traveling north. Built in 1933, that bridge was originally called the North Fork Bridge.

moments.title: Banks
moments.text: Two forks meet at Banks: the North and South forks of the Payette join here, making the community a destination for rafting and kayaking. The meeting also separates two named river runs. The South Fork’s Staircase run ends here, while the Main begins at Banks and parallels Highway 55 downstream to Horseshoe Bend.
moments.notice: The North and South forks of the Payette meet here.
